decisions.reason: Launched only a year ago and shown on its own page, the polymer concrete drain housing remains an uncertain but cheap option that fits the firm's core drainage portfolio, so it is worth keeping open.

The floor-level shower drainage system is a core segment for a drainage specialist and keeping it costs little, though it is only mentioned on the website, so there is not yet enough evidence to justify abandoning it.
The designer shower drainage product has its own page and serves the growing design-bathroom market, so its upside is still uncertain and worth preserving.
The shower element with integrated slope has only a modest website presence, but it complements the shower drain line and costs little to keep while its value is still unresolved.
The backflow-protected basement drain DallSafe 200 is promoted as a specific new development on its own page, which signals a committed, high-potential option to keep.
The air-admittance valve is a low-cost addition to the existing drainage range with little evidence either way, so the option is kept open for now.
